chapter: Wartime South and the Ernie Fields band
title: Drafted and rejected
summary: After a party at Al McKibbon's he is examined for the draft and rejected because of his broken arm; also luck at dice.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: But I want to tell you something that happened before that. I was drafted also. I had turned eighteen, and the draft was on. And I was drafted... So the night that I had to go to the induction center for my examination, the night before rather, they had a big party for me, a going-away party up at Al McKibbon's house. And we had really, really a great time. Anyway, I was sipping the juice pretty good with the party and everything, and I was supposed to be at the place until seven o'clock in the morning, and the party didn't break up until about eight, and my head was spinning. I said, 'I can't go out there like this.' So I just tried to just cool it until I could get my head cleared enough to make it out to the place.

But anyway, we went out there, and I gave them the history of my arm... I mentioned before that I had broken my arm when I was a kid, and I had a double compound fracture in my left arm. It was just my lucky day, because there was two thousand guys there that day, and only two of us came back. The rest of them were inducted. And boy, I almost... I was way out on the East Side of Detroit; I almost walked
all the way home, I felt so good behind that one! [LAUGHS]

Yeah. I think it was just my lucky day more than anything else, you know. Because they had a little dice game at the party, and we started playing penny dice, and I broke everybody, won everybody's money in the house. And the dice never went out. I'd throw them up against the wall any kind of way, and they just wouldn't go out. The thing was just on me, you know. [LAUGHS]
